title: Runtime micro-probing and prioritized kernel selection for mixed-seqlen workloads
creator: Alex Kim
description:
Background: Mixed-sequence-length traffic (short chat turns mixed with long document prefill requests) causes a single static kernel choice to underperform: either we optimize for short latency at the cost of long-seq throughput or vice versa. Previous work focused on offline autotuning per-model and per-arch, but rollout is brittle when hardware, batch mix, or quantization changes.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight runtime micro-probe and prioritized kernel list that: (1) performs a tiny micro-benchmark on first requests for a model deployment on a host to estimate relative kernel throughput/latency across candidate kernels; (2) uses seqlen-percentile bucketing (e.g., 50th/90th/99th) from recent telemetry to pick a prioritized kernel list per (model, arch, quantization, seqlen-bin); (3) caches decisions and refreshes probes periodically or on observed latency drift; (4) applies conservative hysteresis and rollback to avoid oscillation and tail regressions.

Key differences from earlier autotune approaches: the microprobe is runtime and host-local (no heavy offline grid search), prioritization is percentile-driven rather than single-length, and switching cost (KV cache invalidation, warm-start penalty) is explicitly modeled so we only switch when expected ROI exceeds threshold.

Design details:
- Microprobe: 10 inference steps with synthetic prefix/decoder work matching target seqlen-bin; uses non-intrusive scheduling priority and times kernel hot-path only. Probe duration <= 200ms total.
- Decision store: ephemeral host-local cache keyed by (model-hash, device-type, quantization, seqlen-bin, runtime-flag-version). TTL: 10 minutes, refresh on N requests or 10% latency drift.
- Seqlen bucketing: compute online percentiles from last 5k requests per model across the region, push seeds to hosts for initial warm-start.
- Guard rails: minimum sample count 50 before switching; fallback to stable kernel if P95 increases > 5% vs baseline.
- Observability: emit events kernel_probe.*, kernel_choice.*, kernel_switch.* with context fields for later analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
- Feature gated rollout with runtime flag.
- End-to-end integration tests covering probe success/failure and rollback behavior.
- Perf target: for mixed workloads (short+long mix), median latency reduced by >= 10% and cost-per-token decreased by >= 6% on A100 and T4 baselines within canary cohort. No P95 regression > 5% for any rollout host.
- Telemetry: dashboards for probe success rate, switch frequency, per-kernel latency distributions, and rollback events.

Implementation plan / milestones:
1) Prototype microprobe harness + local decision cache (Spike) - 2026-03-05 (done).
2) Integrate seqlen-percentile exporter and host seeding - 2026-03-12 (in progress).
3) Add telemetry events + dashboard panels - 2026-03-18.
4) Canary rollout behind flag (10% hosts) - 2026-03-24.
5) Expand to 50% after 1 week stable metrics - 2026-04-01.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- Probing overhead could add small latency for new model hosts; mitigated by running probe at low priority and only once per TTL.
- Quantized kernels sometimes have large warm-start penalties (KV cache miss) that microprobe may not expose; we'll include a warm-start probe variant.
- Telemetry lag could cause stale seeding on bursty traffic; use conservative TTLs and fallback policy.

Docs/artifacts:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Runtime+microprobe+kernel+chooser
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
- Load test results (canary): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/Runtime/probe-canary-2026-03

Next steps: finalize PR feedback, complete telemetry schema, schedule canary with infra team and SRE for observability support.

2026-03-04 - Priya Desai: Implemented percentile exporter that aggregates per-model seqlen histograms. Sending seeds via config agent to hosts for faster warm-start. Initial integration tests added.
2026-03-06 - Miguel Ortiz (SRE): Requested that probes run on a low-priority QoS class to avoid contention during peak. Also asked for circuit breaker when host CPU > 70%.

2026-03-08 - Priya Desai: Microprobe PR updated with CPU throttle and circuit breaker. Ran short canary on 5 hosts: median latency improvement 12% for mixed workload, but one host saw P95 spike due to quantized kernel warm-start penalty.

2026-03-09 - Sara Liu (Perf Eng): Investigated the P95 spike. Root cause: probe used cold KV cache profile; quantized kernel had high warm-start overhead on long-seq decode. Proposal: add warm-start probe variant that simulates prefix caching and weight-mapped KV state.

2026-03-10 - Priya Desai: Added warm-start probe and hysteresis (min hold 5 minutes). Updated acceptance tests. Scheduling canary with infra for 2026-03-12. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521#issuecomment-8987
